about.intro_content: Prof. Qing-Qing Cai is Deputy Chief of the Department of Medical Oncology at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center (SYSUCC), Guangzhou. She has more than 20 years of clinical oncology experience specialising in lymphoma, nasopharyngeal carcinoma and head and neck squamous cell carcinoma.
about.detailed_content: Prof. Cai leads the Lymphoma Group of the Guangdong Medical Association and received the 2020 People's Good Doctor (Lymphoma) Outstanding Contribution Award and recognition as one of Guangdong Province's first-batch Outstanding Young Medical Talents. In the past 5 years she has published 17 articles as corresponding or co-corresponding author in journals including Blood, Leukemia, Clinical Cancer Research and Signal Transduction and Targeted Therapy, and has led multiple national and provincial research grants. Her research spans NK/T-cell lymphoma immunochemotherapy combinations and prognostic gene signatures for T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma.

faq.section_heading: Frequently Asked Questions About Prof. Qing-Qing Cai

items.question: Does Prof. Qing-Qing Cai accept international patients?
items.answer: CancerFax can coordinate medical report review and consultation support for international patients seeking an opinion related to lymphoma at Sun Yat-sen University Cancer Center, subject to hospital availability and case acceptance.

items.question: What is Prof. Cai's area of specialisation?
items.answer: Prof. Cai specialises in the clinical, translational and basic research of lymphoma, particularly NK/T-cell lymphoma and T-cell lymphoblastic lymphoma, and also conducts clinical research in nasopharyngeal and head and neck cancer.

items.question: How can I request a consultation or second opinion?
items.answer: Submit your medical reports through CancerFax. The CancerFax team reviews the documents, prepares the case for submission, and coordinates next steps with SYSUCC's International Medical Center, subject to availability.

items.question: Is Prof. Cai involved in clinical trials for lymphoma?
items.answer: Yes. Prof. Cai has led and published research on novel immunochemotherapy combinations, including anti-PD-1 antibody plus P-GEMOX chemotherapy, for advanced NK/T-cell lymphoma.

items.question: What awards has Prof. Cai received for her lymphoma work?
items.answer: Prof. Cai received the 2020 People's Good Doctor (Lymphoma) Outstanding Contribution Award and was named among Guangdong Province's first-batch Outstanding Young Medical Talents.
